_comment: Single source of truth for the six dimension hub pages (/models/<slug>/). Rules are evaluated against src/content/models/*.md frontmatter by scripts/generate-hubs.mjs (authoritative membership) and independently re-evaluated by scripts/check-entity-counts.py (verification). Never edit member lists by hand.

hubs.title: Open-weight Chinese AI models
hubs.description: Chinese AI models with openly downloadable weights: licenses, context windows and self-hosting status, counted automatically from the models database.
hubs.short_answer: Open-weight models publish their trained weights for download and self-hosting, unlike API-only models. The database records open-weight status and license terms per model so builders can evaluate deployment rights against the actual license — MIT, Apache-2.0, or a custom regime.
hubs.why_it_matters: The license, not the weights alone, decides what you can legally do: MIT and Apache-2.0 are permissive, while the custom regimes (Kimi K3, MiniMax M-series, Qwen3.8) attach revenue or attribution thresholds.

guides.title: Open-Weight vs API: Trade-offs for Chinese Models
Self-Hosting Chinese Open-Weight Models: Licenses, Hardware and Quantization

research.title: Chinese AI Model Licensing Explained: MIT, Apache and the Three Custom Regimes
Open Weights and API Models in China's 2026 Ecosystem: A Structural Analysis

hubs.title: Long-context Chinese AI models (1M tokens)
hubs.description: Chinese AI models with a documented context window of one million tokens or more, counted automatically from the models database.
hubs.short_answer: Long-context models accept a million or more input tokens in a single request — enough for whole-repository code review, multi-document analysis and long agent traces. This hub lists models whose documented context window is 1,000,000 tokens or more.
hubs.why_it_matters: Input context is cheap to advertise but the output ceiling and cache pricing decide real cost. Output limits range from 131,072 (GLM, Qwen) to 1,048,576 (Kimi K3) tokens — the difference between reading a long document and generating one.

guides.title: Long-Context Model Selection: 1M-Token Windows and What They Actually Mean

research.title: Context Windows in China's 2026 Model Market: 1M Tokens as Table Stakes and the Stratification Below It

hubs.title: Multimodal Chinese AI models
hubs.description: Chinese AI models that accept vision input, with video and computer-use flags shown where documented, counted automatically from the models database.
hubs.short_answer: Multimodal models accept non-text input — images, and in some cases video or screen control. This hub lists every model that records a vision-input flag, with the rarer video and computer-use flags shown where documented.
hubs.why_it_matters: Vision has migrated down the price stack: the cheapest tiers are now among the most capable, and two flagships (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.3) are text-only while their $0.15 flash siblings carry vision.

guides.title: Choosing a Multimodal Chinese Model: Vision, Video and Computer Use

research.title: Multimodal Capability in China's 2026 Model Lineup: Vision, Video and the Computer-Use Frontier

hubs.title: Reasoning Chinese AI models
hubs.description: Chinese AI models that record a reasoning capability flag, counted automatically from the models database.
hubs.short_answer: Reasoning models interleave an extended chain-of-thought before answering, improving performance on math, code and hard knowledge tasks at the cost of latency and output tokens. This hub lists every model that records a reasoning capability flag.
hubs.why_it_matters: Reasoning is near-universal across the 2026 lineup. The real differentiators are whether it can be disabled, its effort levels (low/high/max) and its price — not whether it exists.

guides.title: How to Choose a Chinese AI Model: A Decision Framework

hubs.title: Coding Chinese AI models
hubs.description: Chinese AI models with a documented coding capability flag, counted automatically from the models database.
hubs.short_answer: Coding models are documented for code generation and agentic software work — the arena where China's frontier race is most intense. This hub lists every model that records a coding capability flag.
hubs.why_it_matters: Coding evidence is unevenly published: SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench versions differ across vendors, so the coding flag plus each model's documented benchmark scores is the honest signal set — not a single ranking.

guides.title: Choosing a Chinese Coding Model: SWE Evidence, Tool Calling and Context

research.title: Chinese AI Coding Models: The Agent-Led Race

hubs.title: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Chinese AI models
hubs.description: Chinese AI models documented as Mixture-of-Experts, by explicit architecture label or published active-parameter count, counted automatically from the models database.
hubs.short_answer: Mixture-of-Experts models route each token through a small subset of a much larger parameter set, cutting per-token compute cost. This hub lists models documented as MoE — either by an explicit MoE architecture label or by a published active-parameter count (the sparse-activation signature only MoE models publish).
hubs.why_it_matters: Active parameters, not total, drive inference cost. Activation ratios from ~1.4% (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) to ~5.6% (GLM-5.3-Flash) are a leading indicator of long-run price floors.
hubs.rule_description: architecture contains "MoE" or "Mixture-of-Experts" (case-insensitive) OR parameter_information.active_parameters is present

research.title: How Chinese Frontier Models Use Mixture-of-Experts: Active Parameters, Linear Attention and the Economics of Sparsity
